evidence.quote: initially received Abiraterone and monthly zoledronic acid injection.

A 76-year-old male, a known case of metastatic carcinoma of the prostate (Gleason score: 5 + 5 = 10, grade group 5 with neuroendocrine differentiation) for 1 year, initially received Abiraterone and monthly zoledronic acid injection. He presented to us with rising prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels (137 ng/mL, reference range: <4 ng/mL).

additional_evidence.quote: At 16 months, he then presented with complaints of lower abdominal pain, loss of appetite, and blood in stool.

At 12 months, 68 Gallium-prostate–specific membrane antigen PET/computed tomography ( 68 Ga-PSMA PET/CT) showed extensive osteosclerotic lesions, some of which showed moderate- to high-grade PSMA expression, while others were nontracer avid. There was low-grade diffuse PSMA expression in the prostate gland. He was advised for 177 Lutetium PSMA radioligand therapy ( 177 Lu-PSMA RLT).

At 12 months, 68 Gallium-prostate–specific membrane antigen PET/computed tomography ( 68 Ga-PSMA PET/CT) showed extensive osteosclerotic lesions, some of which showed moderate- to high-grade PSMA expression, while others were nontracer avid. There was low-grade diffuse PSMA expression in the prostate gland. He was advised for 177 Lutetium PSMA radioligand therapy ( 177 Lu-PSMA RLT).

An 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT ( 18 F-FDG PET/CT) was done. It showed mild- to moderate-grade metabolic activity in the multiple osteosclerotic lesions. There was no significant metabolic activity noted in the prostate. 68 Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT was done in view of neuroendocrine differentiation. It showed low-grade somatostatin receptor (SSTR) expression in the multiple osteosclerotic lesions.

An 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT ( 18 F-FDG PET/CT) was done. It showed mild- to moderate-grade metabolic activity in the multiple osteosclerotic lesions. There was no significant metabolic activity noted in the prostate. 68 Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT was done in view of neuroendocrine differentiation. It showed low-grade somatostatin receptor (SSTR) expression in the multiple osteosclerotic lesions.

An 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT ( 18 F-FDG PET/CT) was done. It showed mild- to moderate-grade metabolic activity in the multiple osteosclerotic lesions. There was no significant metabolic activity noted in the prostate. 68 Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT was done in view of neuroendocrine differentiation. It showed low-grade somatostatin receptor (SSTR) expression in the multiple osteosclerotic lesions.

At 16 months, he then presented with complaints of lower abdominal pain, loss of appetite, and blood in stool. Colonoscopy revealed an ulcerative lesion 14 cm from the anal verge. Serum carcinoembryonic antigen levels were raised (102.6 ng/mL, normal 0–2.5 ng/mL). Biopsy revealed adenocarcinoma with focal signet ring cell morphology. He was advised for 68 Ga-fibroblast activation protein inhibitor PET/CT ( 68 Ga-FAPI PET/CT) in view of signet ring cell carcinoma. It showed high-grade fibroblast activation protein (FAP) expression in the heterogeneously enhancing circumferential wall thickening in the sigmoid colon with surrounding serosal irregularity and few tiny pericolonic lymph nodes. Low-grade FAP expression was seen in the known metastatic osteosclerotic lesions from primary prostate malignancy.

MIP images ( A ) showing multiple focal areas of tracer uptake with varying intensity on PSMA, FDG, DOTATATE, and FAPI. field_by_field_audit.source_decisions: Chief complaint is explicitly stated and proposed. Care setting, subject state and other context attributes not explicitly reported; do not invent a clinic or inpatient setting.
Age76 and male documented. No race/ethnicity/residence/anthropometrics or exact birth date reported.

Both confirmed cancers were omitted despite oncology rows. Proposed explicit condition names/site/verification/basis. No NEPC diagnosis inferred from general discussion; status of other diseases unreported.

Three symptoms at16months documented; lower-abdominal body_site proposed. Severity/duration/scores/function not reported. No attribution of appetite-loss site or bleeding anatomy beyond blood in stool.

All named agents represented, including delivered Lu177 dose200mCi,3cycles/every8weeks, zoledronic injection/monthly. Unstated drug doses/routes/stop dates remain null. No false dose transfer from Lu177 to apalutamide.
No patient-specific allergy assessment reported; not_documented appropriate.

Performed PET examinations missing. Proposed four actual procedures while preserving recommendation and subsequent result distinction; colonoscopy/biopsy already present. No device or complication information reported.

Reported PSA/CEA, PET results, negative prostate FDG result and pathology preserved. Method/body_site/serum specimen can be enriched as proposed. No lab draw dates beyond explicitly phase-linked clinical narrative; no numeric uptake or graph data invented.

Two tumor objects and planned+given Lu177 already correct. Add three named cancer therapies and two biomarker entries. Prostate grading/histology/bone extent documented. No T/N/M or formal stage/system/edition/line/intent reported; response progression remains time-specific treatment/outcome, not flattened into initial tumor status.
No actual patient genomic testing, family history, inheritance or consanguinity reported; molecular profiling discussion is background.
No relevant patient reproductive/perinatal findings reported; not_documented appropriate.
No patient-specific exposures or social history reported. General elderly/noninvasive-care rationale is not an index-patient social fact.

PSA progression and after-two-cycle new skeletal lesions are explicit; preserve event6kind outcome. No death/discharge or laterfollowup outcome reported. Postscan progression should also be a supported deterioration outcome in addition to imaging result.
Explicit RLT and FAPI recommendations omitted; proposed recommended-status rows, without inferring counseling/appointments/follow-up orders.
